name: Bartholomew
bio: Bartholomew was one of the twelve apostles Jesus named and sent out with authority to heal and cast out demons, instructed to go first to Israel rather than Gentiles or Samaritans (Matthew 10:1-5). John's Gospel, which never mentions Bartholomew by that name but instead narrates Philip bringing a man named Nathanael to Jesus in the same role the Synoptics give Bartholomew, is traditionally understood to describe the same apostle under his personal name. When Philip told Nathanael he had found the one Moses and the prophets wrote of, Nathanael skeptically asked whether anything good could come out of Nazareth, but came anyway; Jesus, before even being introduced, said he had seen him under a fig tree, prompting Nathanael to declare him the Son of God and King of Israel. Jesus told him he would see even greater things, including heaven opened and angels ascending and descending on the Son of Man (John 1:43-51).
